title: Vector Databases — Find a Neighbor Without Scanning the World
key_insight: A vector database stores vectors in an index built for nearest-neighbor search. It quickly returns items whose vectors are close to the query.
body:
## Find a Neighbor Without Scanning the World

A million documents each have an embedding. Comparing a query with every document works, but becomes too slow for an interactive answer.

A vector database stores vectors in an index built for nearest-neighbor search. It quickly returns items whose vectors are close to the query.

Store the original text and useful metadata beside each vector. The vector finds candidates; the metadata explains and filters them.
common_mistakes: A vector database removes the need to store source text.
Approximate search is guaranteed to return the exact same neighbors.
Access control should be applied only after private text reaches the model.
mini_exercise: Draw “Find a Neighbor Without Scanning the World” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Large retrieval systems need fast similarity search plus filters, updates, metadata, and operational guarantees.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Find a Neighbor Without Scanning the World,” explain Vector Databases without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
